gap: THE TOTALS ROW IS FIXED AND I WILL NOT RE-LITIGATE IT. The hero now prints 'Total' beside $20,324.90, the second mock prints 'الإجمالي' beside the identical figure, and the five locale strings in index.astro carry the same neutral word. The number no longer makes an accounting claim its own rows disprove: two Paid rows and one Draft row can sit under a Total, they could never sit under a Total outstanding. That was r10's decisive fault and it is dead. The currency toggle also moved correctly. USD/EUR/AED now leads the toolbar at (939,386) exactly as Wave's 'All Accounts $25,980.23' selector leads its own Transactions toolbar, and the chip vacated the module rail, covering no module and no panel title. Both changes were real. THE THIRD CHANGE WAS NOT MADE, AND IT WAS HANDED TO ME AS DONE. The claim was 'ALL THREE STATUSES ARE NOW PILLS'. On the served build the hero's Paid badge computes to background-color: rgba(0, 0, 0, 0). Not a pale fill I judged too weak, not a taste call: transparent, read from getComputedStyle on the live DOM, on both Paid rows. Its class list is 'inline-block rounded-pill px-1.5 py-0.5 text-[9px] font-bold bg-mint text-emerald-700'. `bg-mint` emits no CSS because mint is declared in tailwind.config.js as a scale only (100/200/500/700/900) with no DEFAULT key, so there is no .bg-mint rule anywhere in the served stylesheet /_astro/_slug_.CIngtLMO.css. The badge keeps its pill radius and its 2px 6px padding and renders as bare green text on cream, which is precisely the r10 fault. Overdue and Draft, on bg-red-100 and the beige, do fill. So the hero still draws one status as a chip and another as loose text. THIS IS FATAL BECAUSE THE OTHER PANEL IS RIGHT AND IS ON THE SAME PAGE. AppMockup.astro owns a working map: paid 'bg-emerald-50 text-emerald-600', overdue 'bg-copper-50 text-copper-400', draft 'bg-paper-200 text-ink-500'. Every one of those tokens exists and every one renders, so at 2x the Arabic mock shows مدفوعة on a filled mint pill, متأخرة on a peach pill and مسودة on a beige pill, four of four. The hero did not import that map. It hand-wrote a third status vocabulary, and one of its three tokens does not exist. The result is that TWO of the three statuses now disagree between the two mocks, not one: Paid is transparent in the hero and mint-filled in the mock, and Overdue is red-100/red-700 in the hero against copper-50/copper-400 in the mock, a different hue family entirely. The headline directly above the second mock reads 'Your data stays the same, only the interface changes.' r9 forced the two panels to agree on the numbers and they do. r10 forced them to agree on what the number means and they now do. The one thing left that differs between them is the status chrome, which is the exact thing the sentence promises does not differ. A buyer who scrolls from hero to that section sees the same invoice list, the same four customers, the same four amounts, the same Total, and a badge drawn two ways. Wave never exposes this surface because it ships one panel and photographs it. Its equivalent line, 'All Accounts $25,980.23', is a fact its rows cannot contradict, and it has no second panel to contradict its first. SECOND, the currency chip still names a control it does not touch, and the geometry got longer, not shorter. Measured from the DOM: the chip box sits at (729,596) 118x61, so its right-edge tail leaves at roughly (847,627) and lands in empty beige sidebar about 71 CSS px short of the sidebar-to-table divider, at the vertical level of the Total row. The USD/EUR/AED toggle it names is now at (939,386), center (992,400). That is 227 CSS px up and 145 across, and the tail points at neither the toggle nor the Total figure, it points into nothing. The sibling chip proves the idiom works when aimed: 'Languages supported / 5' sits at (738,232) with height 61, so its tail leaves at y=293 and lands on the navy header's globe+EN control. One chip is aimed at a real control, the other is not, which is the same half-honoured idiom r10 recorded. THIRD, mobile is unchanged. Our phone fold carries one complete chip ('Languages supported / 5') plus a truncated navy corner reading 'Invoices EN', with no row, no amount and no status above the fold. Wave's carries two complete legible tag chips, 'Main Street Reno Project' and 'Summer Campaign'. Two finished elements still beat one finished element and a sliver. I said in r10 that a synthetic mock can win and that our own second mock proves it, and I hold to that: the Arabic panel is still the strongest single artefact on either page, a true RTL flip with the Latin customer names holding place while the columns reverse. It loses this round because the flagship panel beside it ships a class that emits no CSS, under a source comment on line 357 asserting 'All three statuses are PILLS', a comment the render disproves. That is the second intent-versus-render gap in this one file, after the currency chip comment r10 caught. THE FIX, in priority order: delete the hero's private status map in src/pages/[...locale]/index.astro and import the working one from src/components/blocks/AppMockup.astro so both panels resolve from a single object. That kills the dead bg-mint and the red-versus-copper split in one edit and removes the possibility of a fourth vocabulary appearing later. If the map must stay local, it is bg-mint-100, never bg-mint, and Overdue must become bg-copper-50 text-copper-400 to match. Verify by asserting getComputedStyle(badge).backgroundColor is not rgba(0, 0, 0, 0) for all three statuses in both mocks, because this fault was invisible to a screenshot read at page scale and only a computed-style check catches the next one. Second, re-anchor the currency chip so its tail terminates on the USD/EUR/AED toggle the way the languages chip terminates on the globe+EN control, or rename the chip to describe what its tail actually reaches. Third, lift the panel so the phone fold shows one complete row with its amount and its status pill.
